public_rationale: Persistent hallucinations are well established, including for GPT-5. Earlier primary studies also document substantial physical and social reasoning failures. But this record does not settle the stronger claim that late-2025 systems were 'not even close' across all the referenced concerns. The studies also show meaningful improvements and sensitivity to prompting. Supporting persistence alone would leave part of Marcus's wording untested.
limitations: Benchmark error rates do not directly measure universal understanding or deployment reliability.
The evidence spans different model generations and evaluation methods.
The statement does not define scaling or proximity to a solution.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Scaling has not come close to solving the reliability, world-understanding and hallucination problems of ChatGPT.

statement.excerpt: Ever since then, thousands of people (literally) have tried to tell me that scaling would solve all these concerns – but it hasn’t. Not even close.
statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

from_speaker: scaling would solve all these concerns
our_interpretation: The referenced concerns are unreliable answers, physical and psychological understanding, and hallucinations.
The observation covers development since December 2022 through publication. It is not a forecast about what scaling could eventually achieve.
The ordinary reading is that these remained substantial practical limitations despite model development, while allowing the improvements Marcus expressly acknowledges elsewhere.
Documenting one remaining error is insufficient to establish 'not even close'.
The personal assertion about thousands of interlocutors is outside the supplied normalized proposition.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations available for models through publication show substantial recurring failures across the referenced areas, sufficient to establish continued practical unreliability rather than isolated residual mistakes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad and reproducible evaluations show that scaled contemporary models have attained dependable performance across the referenced areas, or that the remaining limitations are minor under a defensible ordinary reading.

evidence.explanation: Contemporary models showed substantial errors on this challenging summarization benchmark. The redesigned dataset is harder than its predecessor, so the reported rates cannot establish deterioration over time.
OpenAI confirms that GPT-5 has not eliminated hallucinations. Its acknowledgment of substantial improvement also limits any reading that little progress occurred.
PhyX reports substantial physical-reasoning gaps for GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet and o4-mini. It does not evaluate the later GPT-5 generation.
Models could identify mental states while failing to apply them consistently to behavior. Targeted interventions substantially improved performance, and the study predates the late-2025 frontier.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Versioned evaluations of late-2025 systems across hallucination, physical reasoning and applied social reasoning, with explicit practical reliability standards and enough training information to assess the role of scaling.
